actions.description: Measure optical or radiant intensity at a declared wavelength or channel and return the value with its unit and integration time.

inputs.description: Shutter/integration time of a new frame in milliseconds; converted to the whole microseconds the firmware's clock command takes. Leave it out to read the current buffer
inputs.name: integration_ms

inputs.description: Wavelength in nanometres; the driver reads the pixel whose calibrated coordinate nearest matches it. Leave it out to read the brightest pixel
inputs.name: wavelength_nm

actions.name: measure_intensity

actions.description: Set the firmware sync holdoff time, the delay the firmware's 'set holdoff usecs' command configures (help.txt:82)
actions.name: set_holdoff

outputs.description: Holdoff time written to the firmware, in microseconds
outputs.name: holdoff_us

facts.text: The design is based on the Toshiba TCD1304 (3648/3694 pixels)
The device appears as a serial port with commands and responses in ASCII and frames returned as binary or formatted
The controller writes each command followed by a newline and reads lines until a line starts with DONE
On connect the controller sends stop, reads the identifier and reads the configuration line
The configuration line carries PIXELS, DARK, INVERT and SENSOR, and optionally VPERBIT, BITS and VFS
The reader scales each ADC sample by vperbit and subtracts the mean of the first darklength samples when baseline subtraction is on
A completed frame is queued as [[data], shutter, interval, clock, counter, outercounter, frames, sets, every, mode, elapsed, 0, timestamp]
The clock command takes the shutter time in microseconds: 'clock <n> <shutter>' reads n frames
The stop command stops clocks, triggers and gate
The send command sends the contents of the current buffer
The holdoff time is set with 'set holdoff usecs'
The full detector record has 12 dummy outputs, 13 light-shielded elements, 3 shadowed elements, 3648 effective elements and 14 dummy elements
The master clock is 800 kHz to 4 MHz and the data readout rate is one quarter of it, 200 kS/s to 1 MS/s (500 kS/s below 4 V)
At a 2 MHz master clock one record takes about 7.4 ms to read; transfer to the host adds 5 ms on a Teensy 3.x and about 120 us on a Teensy 4.x

operator_required.name: measure_intensity
operator_required.reason: the clone states that the clock command takes its shutter time in microseconds (help.txt:49-52) and that one record takes about 7.4 ms to read at a 2 MHz master clock (README.md:186), but states no minimum or maximum integration time; the site supplies the range of its detector

operator_required.name: measure_intensity
operator_required.reason: the clone maps pixel numbers to a calibrated coordinate only through coefficients supplied by the device at runtime (TCD1304Rev2Controller.py:602-620, 669-684); it states no wavelength range, so the site supplies the calibrated range of its spectrometer

operator_required.name: set_holdoff
operator_required.reason: the clone states that the firmware holdoff command takes microseconds (help.txt:82) but states no minimum or maximum; the site supplies the holdoff range of its timing setup

safe_state.description: readout and clocking stopped by the firmware 'stop' command
